researcher_notes: No source confirms a construction (site-works/ground-breaking) START year for the H-Energy Kakinada FSRU/onshore terminal. Datable milestones found are all pre- or non-construction: Port Service Agreement with Kakinada Seaports signed 6 Sep 2019; Andhra Pradesh govt permission for the maritime board to issue a comfort letter for BUILDING the Rs 1,600 crore terminal in July 2021 (a permit, not a ground-breaking); and the 2024 IGU report describing it as 'under construction, completion expected 2026'. Company site perennially said 'commissioning by mid-2024'. No ground-breaking ceremony or dated construction commencement is reported by any independent source, so the construction-start year cannot be defensibly assigned. NOTE: distinct from the separate 'Crown Kakinada LNG Terminal' (Crown LNG / Aker Solutions FEED, 2021) - do not conflate.

No source dates a DISTINCT Phase II (onshore/land-based 8 mtpa terminal) proposal. Across sources the Jaigarh project is described as a two-phase development: Phase I = jetty-based FSRU (~4 mtpa; jetty construction began end-2016, Hoegh Giant FSRU arrived Mar 2021/commissioned Mar 2022), and Phase II = conversion to a land-based regasification terminal with ultimate 8 mtpa capacity (two 190,000 m3 tanks), consistently characterized only as 'to be implemented after the successful completion and stabilization of Phase I' with no standalone proposal year. The 8 mtpa onshore endpoint appears in coverage from ~2016-2017 (project launched Dec 2016; indianinfrastructure Jun 2017 cites the 8 mtpa terminal capacity) but never as a datable, discrete Phase II proposal announcement. No page ties a Phase II onshore proposal to a specific year, so no defensible year can be assigned.

FGEN Batangas LNG terminal first publicly proposed in 2018: First Gen signed a Joint Development Agreement with Tokyo Gas on 5 December 2018 to jointly develop the terminal at First Gen's Batangas Clean Energy Complex, and submitted its DOE application (notice to proceed) in December 2018. Confirmed by multiple independent contemporary reports (GMA News, Oil & Gas Journal, LNG Prime, Inquirer). GMA verified to state 'First Gen signed a joint development agreement with Tokyo Gas on December 5, 2018.' Verifier confirms '2018'+'Batangas' present on all four pages.

'retired / substatus planned' = a PLANNED (not-yet-happened) future retirement with NO real date. The BW Batangas is an INTERIM FSRU: FGEN's plan (since the 2019 pivot from onshore to offshore) has always been that the interim FSRU would eventually be REPLACED by a permanent onshore terminal, at which point the FSRU would be retired/demobilized. As of the latest available reporting the FSRU is still in service - it arrived Jun 2023, commissioned Sep 2023, received first cargo Oct 2023, and First Gen was granted a 25-year operating license in January 2025 - and no source gives a target year for retiring the interim FSRU or completing the permanent onshore facility. Per the shard hint, this is a planned retirement with no defensible year -> UNRESOLVED.

Cai Mep LNG terminal (Hai Linh Co., Cai Mep Industrial Zone, Ba Ria-Vung Tau) construction began in 2018 (Q2 2018). GAS SOUTH (pgs.com.vn, a PV Gas subsidiary trade page) states construction of the Hai Linh terminal 'commenced in the second quarter of 2018'; the Vietnamese energy journal nangluongvietnam.vn corroborates a Q2/2018 construction start ('Dự kiến dự án khởi công xây dựng quý 2/2018'). Consistent with physical evidence: S&P Global (Jun 2020) reported construction essentially completed and a test run expected late 2020; storage-tank contract awarded to Lilama 18. Tier=medium/independent=false because one corroborating source frames Q2-2018 as a projection rather than a confirmed ground-breaking, so the two are not fully independent contemporary confirmations - but both point to 2018 and it fits the completed-by-2020 timeline. CAUTION: distinct from the PV Gas 'Thi Vai LNG terminal' (broke ground 28 Oct 2019) at the same Cai Mep-Thi Vai port complex - do not conflate.

Son My LNG terminal (Binh Thuan) first publicly proposed in 2017: AES and PetroVietnam Gas (PV Gas) signed an MOU on 12 November 2017, witnessed by Presidents Trump and Tran Dai Quang during Trump's state visit to Vietnam, to jointly develop the Son My LNG terminal. Confirmed by contemporary independent media (Vietnam Investment Review / vir.com.vn, dated 20 Nov 2017, reporting the MOU 'inked with AES Corporation on November 12') and by AES Vietnam's own press release ('In November 2017, AES signed an MOU with PV Gas... to develop the... Son My LNG Terminal Project'). Independent origins (media + sponsor). Verifier confirms '2017'+'Son My' present on both.
